gate_scope: Design and usability defects: accessibility, layout and the recorded design process, backed by fresh browser evidence. Speed is optional and never blocks this gate. Design quality is judged on the screenshots and by the user.

findings.message: motion-too-sparse at desktop: Only 0 distinct motion idea(s) found across scroll positions and declared animations (need 3 for a calm page, undeclared page with table/grid content, calm threshold): build one scroll- or hand-driven signature set piece from the subject (a pinned stage that changes with scroll counts), or declare <meta name="layoza-motion" content="calm"> if the page is meant to be quiet
findings.remediation: Fewer distinct elements move, transition or follow scroll than the page's declared motion level expects: build one scroll- or hand-driven signature set piece from the subject (then two motion ideas are enough), or declare <meta name="layoza-motion" content="calm"> (or `none`) if a quiet page is intended.

findings.message: Design critique: Overused font at desktop: Primary font: arial (97% of text)
findings.remediation: Inter, Roboto, Fraunces, Geist, Plus Jakarta Sans, and Space Grotesk are used on so many sites they no longer feel distinctive. Each new wave of AI-generated UIs converges on the same handful of faces. Choose a face that gives your interface personality. If the existing brand requires this, declare it with <meta name="layoza-brand-allow" content="font:<family>, palette:<cream|purple|cyan>"> and the rule stands down.

findings.message: Design critique: Cream / beige palette at desktop: cream/beige page background rgb(245, 243, 238)
findings.remediation: A warm cream or beige page background has become the default "tasteful" AI surface, reached for by reflex. Choose a background that comes from a deliberate palette, not the safe warm off-white. If the existing brand requires this, declare it with <meta name="layoza-brand-allow" content="font:<family>, palette:<cream|purple|cyan>"> and the rule stands down.

findings.message: Design critique: Undersized functional text at desktop: 9px functional text "Bakery operations" (below 11px floor) (+9 more)
findings.remediation: Interactive and content-bearing UI text (links, buttons, nav items, labels, table cells, meta rows, timecodes) below 11px is a legibility failure, not a style choice. WCAG sets no absolute pixel floor, but functional text under 11px is a defensible quality bar: it fails on high-DPI and small viewports and it degrades tap and read targets. The 11px floor holds even inside a footer; only non-interactive legal smallprint gets the softer 10px floor. Being ON the DESIGN.md size ramp does not exempt a value here: adding 8px to the ramp launders the token but not the legibility problem, and that is exactly the escape hatch this rule closes. Exempts sup/sub, visually-hidden (sr-only) text, and code/terminal contexts. Decorative letterspaced micro-labels are still functional and stay in scope.

findings.message: Design critique: Tiny body text at desktop: 10px body text <small> "5 batches · 248 pieces" (+3 more)
findings.remediation: Body text below 12px is hard to read, especially on high-DPI screens. Use at least 14px for body content, 16px is ideal.

findings.message: Design critique: Middle-dot meta strings at desktop: 2 meta strings joined with middle dots, e.g. "Classic · 75 g · 96 pieces", "Jamie R. #10422 sourdough · 4 croissants09:30Studio North #104312 morning buns10:00Riley T. #10441 focaccia · 1 rye10:30"
findings.remediation: Meta lines joined with middle dots ('A · B · C') are a recurring generated-page signature. Set the facts in a structure that fits them (a definition list, a table row, a sentence) or keep only the one that matters.

findings.message: Design critique: Dead controls at desktop: 12 of 12 buttons have no transition and no :active press state (e.g. a.skip); give every control hover, press and state feedback (layoza-animations 2c)
findings.remediation: Most buttons have no transition and no :active press state, so clicks feel unacknowledged. Give every control hover, press and state feedback (layoza-animations 2c); under a static brief an instant :active colour change is enough.

findings.message: svg-text-illegible at desktop: 7 SVG text label(s) render under 9px at 1440px after viewBox scaling: "5:00" 8.4px, "6:00" 8.4px, "7:00" 8.4px; enlarge them, hide them at this width, or move the content into HTML
findings.remediation: SVG labels scaled down by the viewBox render under 9px: enlarge them at this width, hide them and carry the content in HTML, or swap to a mobile-specific drawing.

findings.message: heading-crowding at tablet: <h2> "Before the next bake" sits 15px from sibling column <small> "2 low-stock items" (min 16px)
findings.remediation: Increase column gap beside the heading or stack the columns at this width.

findings.message: contrast unmeasurable (image/gradient) for some text, so no ratio is claimed: svg text x7
findings.remediation: Check these by eye or give the text a solid backing (a scrim or a solid panel) so contrast can be measured.

manual_review_required: Verify keyboard Tab/Shift+Tab focus order matches visual reading sequence across 375px, 768px, and 1280px viewports (WCAG 2.4.3).
Verify focus appearance and non-obscuration when sticky headers or dialogs are active (WCAG 2.4.11 / 2.4.13).
Verify screen-reader announcement clarity for dynamic state changes and live regions (WCAG 4.1.3).
accessibility.evidence_basis: browser report (qa/browser-qa-report.json, fast mode) + static checks
needs_browser: Skipped by the browser report: Full rule sweep, craft, tells, interface, design-token and art-over-text checks at 768px, 375px: fast mode ran layout, overflow and touch rules only there; run with --full

core_web_vitals.methodology_disclosure: Measured in one headless Chromium load per viewport (`qa/browser-qa-report.json`): LCP/CLS via PerformanceObserver, INP via an Event Timing proxy. Lab diagnostics, not CrUX field telemetry.
